# Figure legends (generated by scripts/8_audit/h41_main_results_figs.py, 2026-11-06T04:16)

**Fig. 1 | A neck model that largely reproduces published values screens 149 cage designs; none passes every test so far.**
**a**, Side view of the real model: C3 and C4 outer bone and one cage slice. Arrows mark the slip and squeeze the cage must resist. **b**, Our C0-C7 model against the digitised values of Herron et al. 2020 (26-year-old model): 15 of 19 quantities are within 10 %. The four outside are C0-C1 (lateral bending, axial rotation), C1-C2 and C3-C7 (axial rotation). C3-C4 facet forces are within 2 %. This shows that we reproduce a published, validated model; it is not an independent cadaver validation of the implanted state. **c**, Each design is counted once, under its first failed test. Counts: {'compress': 72, 'exc': 28, 'unf': 18, 'shear': 14, 'slip': 17}.

**Fig. 2 | The designs that hold the cage in place overload the hard-soft bond, and the designs that spare the bond slide.**
**a**, 28 distinct designs with both real-friction windows and a bond value. Runs of byte-identical inputs are one design, plotted at its worst slip and worst shear, following the PI rule that any fail in pooled duplicates fails the group. Slip fraction = largest of (translation / 1 mm, backward translation / 0.5 mm) at the evaluation point. Bond shear = soft-side 99th percentile at the intact range-of-motion state. No design is inside both limits. One individual run (['p100']) was inside both, but a run of the same input was not. **b**, Sustained compression of the soft phase, by cage type: {'Other types (threaded faces, both layouts, family B)': (50, 58), 'Softer towards the faces, blended': (3, 21), 'Soft inside, hard ring outside': (0, 58)}. Within a type, softer material is squeezed more. **c**, Glued-model one-face slip bound against real-friction translation at the intact range of motion, physio_fric3.

## Provisional
All friction and bond verdicts are provisional (verdicts.json meta): NUM-16 (bond metric mesh sensitivity, about 16 %), NUM-17 (same input can land on either side of a limit; 3 of 15 repeat pairs), FEBio cage drift that scales with increments at a fixed angle (DECISIONS 2026-11-06 00:50, 2 designs; the earlier density explanation was retracted and the physio_fric4 rerun is held), and a 3 MPa limit that has no PLCL bond-strength data. Evaluated on one 26-year-old model; degradation, fatigue and creep are outside these figures.
